checks: Projection of the finite supporting-slope polyhedron is closed and constant heights are feasible. The nonnegative sampled height sublevels are bounded, so an optimizing height has a feasible slope lift. At any optimizer the homogeneous active cone gives feasible short directions, and finite Farkas gives the specified nonnegative multiplier signs. For q>1 the positive-part extension is differentiable at zero, and for q=1 use the linear extension.

Stationarity in slope space gives the full outgoing row displacement because every p_j-p_i is in that same direction space. The complementary support equations make the outgoing height change zero. Multiplying height balance by h_i and summing yields the qR reward, and the mass and first moments follow by summing that balance without h_i and with p_i respectively.

For q>1 zero-height nodes cannot send to a positive height. Their stationarity sums imply no incoming external flow and no obstacle mass. On this set conservation plus row barycenters forces the sum of squared edge displacements to vanish. Distinct bases remove all remaining internal off-diagonal flow. All-zero and single-node cases are covered.

On retained nodes the positive stop probabilities bound row sums of T below one. Neumann inversion preserves nonnegativity. In row-vector orientation a=λ+aT gives the column masses after multiplication by D, and (I-T)1=D1 and (I-T)p=Dp give the row masses and displacement. Supporting gaps are nonnegative and their matrix integral vanishes using the qR identity, which gives genuine support equality on every positive edge and obstacle equality at its source.

For every feasible matrix the zero row displacements remove the slope terms in the weak-dual bound. The conjugate over nonnegative heights is exactly (q-1)q^(-q')s^q', attained at s=q h^(q-1). The constructed columns give penalty (q-1)R, and q=1 gives unit columns. An exact check at bases -1,0,1 with q=2 and e=(0,1,0) gives h=(1,1,1), λ=(0,6,0), one row (2,2,2), reward 6, penalty 3, and R=3.
